quote.translation: Accordingly the probability that the five planets known at that time should all be so is 24⁻⁵, that is, the small figure of about one in eight million" (Arrhenius, Shiteki ni mitaru kagakuteki uchūkan no hensen, trans. Terada Torahiko, Iwanami Bunko, pp. 138-139).

regions.text: この場合偶然とは一個の遊星について云へば二十四の離接肢の各々が全鐙に對して有つ離接偶然であり、五個の遊星について云へば二十四の五乗である約入百度の離接肢の各々が全體に對して有つ離接前偶然である。

quote.translation: The contingent here, if we speak of one planet, is the disjunctive contingency that each of twenty-four disjuncts has in relation to the whole; if we speak of five planets, it is the disjunctive contingency that each of roughly eight million disjuncts, twenty-four to the fifth power, has in relation to the whole.

regions.text: 以上の諸例によつて、全嗇の中の各部分が單なる可能的離接肢として、全體の必然性に對して離接的偶然を構成することが明かになつたであらう。

quote.translation: These examples will have made it clear that each part within a whole, as a merely possible disjunct, constitutes disjunctive contingency in relation to the necessity of the whole.

regions.text: 離接的偶然にあつて偶然性の問題が可能性の間題に深く織れてあることは明かである。

quote.translation: In disjunctive contingency, plainly, the problem of contingency touches deeply on the problem of possibility.

regions.text: 可能的離接肢の一つの措定が偶然であり偶然であるが故に他の措定も取能である。

quote.translation: The positing of one possible disjunct is contingent, and because it is contingent the positing of another is also possible.

regions.text: 今迄は偶然を必然の反勤概念として取扱つて来たがいつたい偶然は可能に對して如何なる開係に立つか。

quote.translation: Up to now we have treated the contingent as the opposite concept of the necessary; what relation, then, does the contingent bear to the possible?

regions.text: 偶然と可能との開係を攻究する前に、先づ様相性一般に開して考察して置かう。さうして様相性の考察に

quote.translation: Before investigating that relation, let us first consider Modality in general, and in considering Modality we cannot but take Aristotle's classical treatment as our point of departure (Aristoteles, De Interpretatione 12, 13; Metaphysica Δ 5, 12).
